original_question: Let Gamma be a complete intersection numerical semigroup, let R_Gamma = k[[Gamma]], let m be the maximal ideal of R_Gamma, let G_Gamma = gr(R_Gamma), and let HF_{G_Gamma}(j) = dim_k(m^j/m^{j+1}) be the Hilbert function of the associated graded ring. Is this Hilbert function always non-decreasing as j increases?
target_in_paper: Section 7, Problem 28 (Rossi's Problem): let Gamma be a complete intersection numerical semigroup; is its Hilbert function non-decreasing? This is the exact open problem your draft is aiming at. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2406.00790))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right paper target and almost all of its mathematical content: the hypothesis that Gamma is a complete intersection numerical semigroup, the passage to the local semigroup ring k[[Gamma]], the maximal ideal m, the associated graded ring gr_m(R_Gamma), and the Hilbert function HF_{G_Gamma}(j) = dim_k(m^j/m^{j+1}). Section 1 supplies exactly this ring-theoretic setup, and Section 7 asks precisely whether that Hilbert function is non-decreasing for complete intersection numerical semigroups. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2406.00790))
missing_details: State explicitly that k is an arbitrary field, and that R_Gamma means the local semigroup ring k[[t^gamma : gamma in Gamma]] inside k[[t]]. Section 1 fixes the field and defines the local semigroup ring in this way. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2406.00790))

Spell out the quantifier: the problem is whether the monotonicity statement holds for every complete intersection numerical semigroup Gamma, with no extra restriction on embedding dimension or other invariants. Problem 28 is stated in that full generality. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2406.00790))

Make the monotonicity condition fully explicit as HF_{G_Gamma}(j) <= HF_{G_Gamma}(j+1) for all integers j >= 0; the paper phrases this as 'the Hilbert function non-decreasing,' so writing the inequality makes the stand-alone version sharper.

It is important not to add extra assumptions such as Cohen-Macaulayness of G_Gamma. The nearby discussion emphasizes that the problem is interesting precisely because k[[Gamma]] being complete intersection does not force gr_m(R_Gamma) to be complete intersection or even Cohen-Macaulay. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2406.00790))

If you want a paper-faithful equivalent hypothesis, you may replace 'Gamma is a complete intersection numerical semigroup' by the equivalent condition that the local semigroup ring k[[Gamma]] is a complete intersection local ring; Section 7 states this equivalence explicitly. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2406.00790))
refined_question: For every field k and every complete intersection numerical semigroup Gamma, let R_Gamma = k[[t^gamma : gamma in Gamma]] be the local semigroup ring with maximal ideal m, and let G_Gamma = gr_m(R_Gamma) = direct sum over j >= 0 of m^j/m^{j+1}. Must its Hilbert function HF_{G_Gamma}(j) = dim_k(m^j/m^{j+1}) be non-decreasing; equivalently, does HF_{G_Gamma}(j) <= HF_{G_Gamma}(j+1) hold for every j >= 0? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2406.00790))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, if the local semigroup ring k[[Gamma]] is a complete intersection local ring (equivalently, Gamma is a complete intersection numerical semigroup), is the Hilbert function of its associated graded ring gr_m(k[[Gamma]]) non-decreasing? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2406.00790))
justification: This is the nearest official formulation in the paper, with no broadening. Section 1 defines the local semigroup ring and associated graded ring attached to a numerical semigroup. Section 7 then specializes to complete intersection semigroups, recalls the equivalence with the complete intersection property of the semigroup ring/local semigroup ring, and states Problem 28 exactly as the monotonicity of the Hilbert function. The surrounding discussion also fixes the intended scope: the issue is nontrivial because the associated graded ring need not be Cohen-Macaulay; the answer is known to be positive when the embedding dimension is at most 4; and the broader symmetric/Gorenstein version is false, so the paper's true target is specifically the complete intersection case. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2406.00790))
